Moses sent them to the war, a thousand from every tribe, and with them he sent Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, who had in his hand the holy vessels and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They waged war against Midian, as Yahweh had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
They killed the kings of Midian in addition to the others who were slain: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian.{b} They also killed Balaam the son of Beor with the sword.
And the Israelites took the Midianite women and their children captive, and seized all their herds, their flocks, and all their goods as spoil.
They burned all the cities where they had settled, and all their camps,{c} with fire.
They took all the spoil and all the booty, both of humans and of animals.
And they brought the prisoners, along with the booty and the spoil, to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the Israelite congregation, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Moses and Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the congregation went out to meet them outside the camp.
And Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had come from the campaign of the war.
Moses said to them, “Have you let all the women live?
Look, these were the ones who, on Balaam’s advice, caused the Israelites to act unfaithfully against Yahweh in the matter of Peor, so that the plague came on the congregation of Yahweh.
Now therefore, kill every boy among the children, and kill every woman who has had intercourse with a man.
But all the young girls who have not known a man by lying with a male, keep alive for yourselves.
As for you, camp outside the camp seven days. Whoever has killed a person and whoever has touched a slain person, purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
You shall purify every garment, everything made of leather, everything woven of goat hair, and everything made of wood.”{d}
Then Eleazar the priest said to the men of war who had gone to the battle, “This is the statute of the law that Yahweh has commanded Moses:
Only the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin, and the lead,

everything that can withstand fire you shall put through the fire, and it shall be clean; yet it must also be purified with the water of impurity. And anything that cannot withstand fire you shall put through water.
You are to wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean. Afterward you may come into the camp.”
Yahweh said to Moses,
“Take a count of the plunder that was captured, both of people and of animals, you and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the congregation.
Divide the spoil into two portions, between the soldiers who fought in the battle and the rest of the congregation.
And set apart a levy for Yahweh from the soldiers who went out to battle: one in every five hundred, whether of persons, cattle, donkeys, or sheep and goats.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as a contribution to Yahweh.

And from the Israelites’ half you shall take one in every fifty, whether of persons, cattle, donkeys, or sheep and goats—of all the animals—and give them to the Levites, who have charge of Yahweh’s tabernacle.”
And Moses and Eleazar the priest did as Yahweh commanded Moses.
Now the plunder remaining of the spoil that the men of war had taken was 675,000 sheep,
72,000 cattle,
61,000 donkeys,
and 32,000 persons in all, women who had never had intercourse with a man.
The half portion of those who had gone to the war was, in number, 337,500 sheep and goats,
and Yahweh’s tribute of sheep was 675.
The cattle were 36,000, of which Yahweh’s tribute was 72.
The donkeys were 30,500, of which Yahweh’s tribute was 61.
The persons were 16,000, of which Yahweh’s tribute was 32 persons.
And Moses gave the tribute, which was Yahweh’s contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
As for the Israelites’ half, which Moses had separated from the soldiers’ share,
now the congregation’s half was 337,500 sheep,
36,000 cattle,
30,500 donkeys,
and 16,000 persons.
From the Israelites’ half Moses took one portion in fifty, whether human or animal, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of Yahweh’s tabernacle, just as Yahweh had commanded Moses.
Then the officers who were over the thousands of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, came near to Moses
and they said to Moses, “Your servants have taken the count of the soldiers in our charge, and not one of us is lacking.
So we have brought as an offering to Yahweh what each man found of gold ornaments—armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces—to make atonement for ourselves before Yahweh.”
So Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all of it in worked ornaments.
All the gold of the contribution that they presented to Yahweh, from the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, came to about 420 pounds.{e}
(The men of war had taken plunder, each man for himself.)
And Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a reminder of the Israelites before Yahweh.

notes.text: Or “twelve units.” On the Hebrew ’elef, “thousand” or “clan unit,” see the note at 1:46.
Evi perhaps means “desire.” Rekem, “variegated.” Zur, “rock.” Hur, perhaps “white” or “child.” Reba, “fourth” or “offspring.”
Hebrew tirot, walled encampments or circular settlements of tents.
At about this point the Samaritan Pentateuch adds further instructions on purification. See the note at 10:10.
Hebrew “16,750 shekels,” about 193 kilograms. A shekel was about 0.4 ounce (11.5 grams); standards varied.

verses.text: Now the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad had a very great number of livestock. They saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and saw that the place was a place for livestock.
So the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben came and spoke to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to the leaders of the congregation, saying,
“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo, and Beon,{a}
the land that Yahweh struck down before the congregation of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock.”
They continued, “If we have gained your favor, let this land be granted to your servants as our holding; do not bring us over the Jordan.”
But Moses said to the descendants of Gad and to the descendants of Reuben, “Shall your brothers go to the war while you sit here?
Why would you discourage the Israelites from crossing over into the land that Yahweh has given them?
This is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to see the land.
For when they went up to the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, they discouraged the Israelites from going into the land that Yahweh had given them.
And Yahweh’s anger burned on that day, and he swore, saying,
‘Surely none of the men who came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, will see the land that I swore to give to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, because they have not followed me fully,
none except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite{b} and Joshua son of Nun, for they have followed Yahweh fully.’
And Yahweh’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that had done evil in the eyes of Yahweh was gone.
And now here you are, risen up in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinners, adding still more to Yahweh’s burning anger against Israel!
For if you turn away from following him, he will again abandon them in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.”
Then they came near to him and said, “We will build sheepfolds here for our livestock and cities for our little ones,

but we ourselves will take up arms, ready to go before the Israelites, until we have brought them to their place. And our little ones will live in the fortified cities because of the inhabitants of the land.
We will not return to our homes until each of the Israelites has received his inheritance.
For we will not inherit with them on the other side of the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on this side of the Jordan to the east.”
Moses answered them, “If you will carry this out, and arm yourselves to march before Yahweh into battle,
and every armed man of you will cross the Jordan before Yahweh, until he has driven out his enemies from before him
and the land is subdued before Yahweh, then afterward you may return and be free of obligation to Yahweh and to Israel, and this land will be your possession before Yahweh.
But if you will not do so, look, you have sinned against Yahweh, and be sure your sin will find you out.
Build cities for your little ones and folds for your sheep, and do what has come out of your mouth.”
And the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben said to Moses, “Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our livestock will remain there in the cities of Gilead,
but your servants will cross over, every man who is armed for war, before Yahweh to battle, as my lord says.”
So Moses gave command concerning them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun, and to the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the Israelites.

And Moses said to them, “If the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben, every man who is armed to battle before Yahweh, will cross over the Jordan with you and the land is subdued before you, then you are to give them the land of Gilead as a possession.
But if they will not cross over with you armed, they are to have possessions among you in the land of Canaan.”
And the descendants of Gad and the descendants of Reuben answered, “What Yahweh has said to your servants, that we will do.
We will cross over armed before Yahweh into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance will remain with us beyond the Jordan.”

So Moses gave to them, to the descendants of Gad and to the descendants of Reuben and to half the tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, the land with its cities and their territories, the cities of the land throughout.
And the descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Atroth-shophan, Jazer, Jogbehah,
Beth-nimrah, and Beth-haran, fortified cities, and folds for sheep.
And the descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo, Baal Meon (their names were changed), and Sibmah; and they gave other names to the cities they rebuilt.{c}
The sons of Machir the son of Manasseh went to Gilead, captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled in it.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and called them Havvoth-jair.{d}
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and called it Nobah, after his own name.

notes.text: These are towns east of the Jordan. Sebam is probably Sibmah (verse 38), and Beon is Baal-meon (verse 38).
The Kenizzites were a clan descended from Kenaz, an Edomite (Genesis 36:11), who joined Judah.
Nebo and Baal-meon contain names of gods (Nabu and Baal), which may explain the renaming.
Havvoth-jair means “tent villages of Jair.”

verses.text: These are the stages of the journeys of the Israelites, when they came out of the land of Egypt by their divisions under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
Moses wrote down their starting places, stage by stage, at the command of Yahweh. These are their stages according to their starting places.

They departed from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month (in March–April).{a} On the day after the Passover the Israelites marched out boldly{b} in full view of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom Yahweh had struck down among them. On their gods also Yahweh executed judgments.
So the Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
They left Etham and turned back toward Pi Hahiroth, which is east of Baal Zephon, and camped in front of Migdol.
They left Hahiroth{c} and crossed the sea through its midst into the wilderness; they traveled three days in the Wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They left Marah and came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees; and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the Wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the Wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the Wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the Wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.{d}
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the Wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.

Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the command of Yahweh and died there, in the fortieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month (in July–August).{e}
Aaron was a hundred twenty-three years old when he died on Mount Hor.
And the Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard of the coming of the Israelites.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim{f} and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, before Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
They camped by the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim{g} in the plains of Moab.
Yahweh spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then you are to drive out all the inhabitants of the land from before you and destroy all their carved stones,{h} destroy all their metal images, and demolish all their high places.
You are to take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given the land to you to possess.

You are to inherit the land by lot according to your clans. To a large clan you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a small clan you are to give a smaller inheritance. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that is to be his. You are to inherit according to the tribes of your fathers.

But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land ahead of you, those you allow to remain will become barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the land where you live.
And as I thought to do to them, so I will do to you.’”

notes.text: First month: Abib, later called Nisan, of the spring-start religious calendar. Because the months were lunar, the date falls in different parts of March and April from year to year. Compare Exodus 12:2–6, 51.
Hebrew “with a high hand.”
Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient versions read “Pi-hahiroth,” as in verse 7.

Verses 16–36 list stopping places, many of which are found only here and cannot now be located. Some names describe features: Rithmah, “broom bush”; Rimmon-perez, “pomegranate of the breach”; Libnah, “white”; Haradah, “trembling”; Makheloth, “assemblies”; Moseroth, “bonds”; Bene-jaakan, “sons of Jaakan”; Jotbathah, “pleasantness”; Ezion-geber, perhaps “backbone of a man,” at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba.

Fifth month: Av, of the spring-start religious calendar. Because the months were lunar, the date falls in different parts of July and August from year to year. This is the only place in the Bible where the date of Aaron’s death is given.
Iyim, “ruins,” is a short form of Iye-abarim (verse 44).
Beth-jeshimoth means “house of the wastes.” Abel-shittim means “meadow of acacias”; compare Shittim in 25:1.
Or “figured stones,” carved images used in worship.

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Command the Israelites and tell them: When you enter Canaan (this is the land that shall fall to you as an inheritance—Canaan according to its boundaries),
your southern side shall run from the Wilderness of Zin alongside Edom, and your southern boundary shall begin at the eastern end of the Salt Sea;{a}
your border shall turn southward of the Akrabbim Pass,{b} continue on to Zin, and end south of Kadesh Barnea; it shall extend to Hazar Addar and pass along to Azmon;
The border is to turn from Azmon to the Brook of Egypt,{c} and its limit is to be at the sea.
“‘For the western border you are to have the Great Sea{d} and its coast. This is to be your western border.
“‘This is to be your northern border: from the Great Sea you are to mark out your line to Mount Hor.{e}
From Mount Hor you are to mark it out to Lebo-hamath, and the limit of the border is to be at Zedad.
Then the border is to extend to Ziphron, and its limit is to be at Hazar-enan. This is to be your northern border.
“‘You are to mark out your eastern border from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The border is to go down from Shepham to Riblah on the east side of Ain. And the border is to go down and reach the slope east of the Sea of Chinnereth.{f}
And the border is to go down to the Jordan, and its limit is to be at the Salt Sea. This is to be your land with its borders all around.’”
Moses commanded the Israelites, saying, “This is the land that you are to inherit by lot, which Yahweh has commanded to give to the nine tribes and to the half-tribe.
The tribe of Reuben’s sons by their ancestral houses, and the tribe of Gad’s sons by their ancestral houses, and half the tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance.
The two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“These are the names of the men who are to divide the land to you for inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
You shall take one leader from every tribe to apportion the land as an inheritance.
These are the names of the men: Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.
Of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon.
Of the tribe of the descendants of Dan a leader, Bukki son of Jogli.
Of the descendants of Joseph: of the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod.
And of the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan.
Of the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach.
Of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan.
And of the tribe of the descendants of Asher a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi.
Of the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud.{g}
These are the ones whom Yahweh commanded to divide the inheritance to the Israelites in the land of Canaan.”

notes.text: That is, the Dead Sea.
Akrabbim means “scorpions.”
Probably the Wadi el-Arish in northern Sinai.
That is, the Mediterranean Sea.
Not the Mount Hor of 20:22, but a mountain in the north, probably in the Lebanon range.
That is, the Sea of Galilee. Chinnereth may mean “harp-shaped.”

Several of these names are theophoric: Shemuel, “name of God”; Elidad, “God has loved”; Hanniel, “grace of God”; Kemuel, perhaps “assembly of God”; Elizaphan, “God has protected”; Paltiel, “God is my deliverance”; Pedahel, “God has redeemed.” Bukki perhaps means “proved”; Ahihud, “my brother is majesty.”

verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying,
“Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in out of the inheritance they possess; and you shall give the Levites open pastureland around the towns.
The cities are to be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands are to be for their cattle, for their possessions, and for all their animals.
The pasturelands of the cities, which you are to give to the Levites, are to reach from the wall of the city outward 1,500 feet{a} all around.

And you are to measure outside the city, on the east side 3,000 feet,{b} on the south side 3,000 feet, on the west side 3,000 feet, and on the north side 3,000 feet, with the city in the middle. This is to be the pastureland of their cities.
“The towns you give the Levites shall include the six cities of refuge, which you shall designate for a killer to flee to; and in addition you shall give forty-two towns.
All the cities that you give to the Levites are to be forty-eight cities with their pasturelands.

As for the cities that you give from the possession of the Israelites, from the larger tribes you are to take many, and from the smaller tribes you are to take few. Each is to give some of its cities to the Levites, in proportion to the inheritance that it receives.”
Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the Israelites and say to them, ‘When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
then you are to select cities to be cities of refuge for you, so that the manslayer who kills any person unintentionally may flee there.
The cities are to be for you a refuge from the avenger,{c} so that the manslayer may not die until he stands before the congregation for judgment.
The cities that you give are to be your six cities of refuge.
Three cities you shall give on this side of the Jordan, and three cities in the land of Canaan; they shall be cities of refuge.
These six cities are to be for refuge for the Israelites, and for the foreigner and the resident alien among them, so that anyone who kills a person unintentionally may flee there.
“But if he strikes him with an iron tool so that he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
And if he strikes him with a stone held in the hand, of a size that could kill, and he dies, he is a murderer; the murderer shall surely be put to death.
Or if he struck him down with a wooden object in the hand, by which a man may die, and he died, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself is to put the murderer to death. When he meets him, he is to put him to death.
Or if in hatred he shoves him, or hurls something at him from ambush so that he dies,
or in enmity hits him with his fist and he dies, the one who hit him is to be put to death, for he is a murderer; the avenger of blood shall kill the murderer upon meeting him.
“‘But if he pushed him suddenly without enmity, or threw anything at him without lying in wait,
or, using any stone that could kill, drops it on him without seeing him, so that he dies, though he was not his enemy and was not seeking his harm,
then the congregation shall decide between the one who struck and the blood avenger on the basis of these rules.

The congregation shall rescue the killer from the avenger of blood, and the congregation shall return him to his city of refuge where he had fled; and he shall live there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer ever leaves the boundary of the city of refuge where he fled,
and the blood avenger finds him outside the boundary of his city of refuge and kills the slayer, no bloodguilt attaches to him,
because the killer must stay in his city of refuge until the high priest dies; only after the high priest’s death may the slayer go back to his own landed property.
These shall be a legal ordinance for you through all your generations, wherever you live.
“If anyone kills a person, the murderer shall be put to death at the word of witnesses; but one witness alone cannot testify against a person to bring about his death.
Moreover, you are to accept no ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty of death. He must be put to death.
And you shall take no ransom for someone who has fled to his city of refuge, to allow him to go back and live on his land before the high priest dies.
Do not pollute the land you are in, for blood pollutes the land, and the land cannot be atoned for regarding the blood poured out in it, except by the blood of the person who poured it out.
Do not make unclean the land where you live, in whose midst I dwell; for I, Yahweh, dwell among the Israelites.”

notes.text: Hebrew “a thousand cubits,” about 450 meters. A cubit was about 18 inches (45 centimeters).
Hebrew “two thousand cubits,” about 900 meters. The relation between verses 4 and 5 is uncertain; verse 5 may give the length of each side of a square around the city.
Hebrew go’el, the nearest relative, responsible for avenging a killing. See the note at 5:8.

verses.text: The family heads of the clan of Gilead’s descendants, the son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the Joseph clans, came near and spoke in the presence of Moses and the leaders, the family heads of the Israelites.

They said, “Yahweh commanded my lord to distribute the land by lot as an inheritance to the Israelites, and my lord was commanded by Yahweh to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

Yet if they marry sons from another Israelite tribe, their inheritance will be removed from our ancestral inheritance and added to the inheritance of the tribe they join; thus it will be cut off from the allotment of our inheritance.
And when the Israelites’ Jubilee{a} arrives, their inheritance will be added to that of the tribe they have joined, and their inheritance will be cut off from our ancestral tribe’s inheritance.”
So Moses commanded the Israelites according to the word of Yahweh, saying, “The tribe of the descendants of Joseph is right.
This is the command of Yahweh for Zelophehad’s daughters: they may marry anyone they choose, but only within a family of their father’s tribe.
The inheritance of the Israelites is not to pass from tribe to tribe, for every one of the Israelites is to hold on to the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers.
Every daughter who holds an inheritance in any Israelite tribe shall marry someone from a family of her father’s tribe, so that each Israelite keeps his ancestral inheritance.
No inheritance shall be transferred from one tribe to another, for the Israelite tribes shall each keep to their own inheritance.’”
The daughters of Zelophehad did as Yahweh commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, Zelophehad’s daughters, married their cousins on their father’s side.
They were married into the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained in the tribe of their father’s clan.
These are the commands and ordinances that Yahweh gave to the Israelites through Moses on the plains of Moab by the Jordan across from Jericho.

notes.text: The Jubilee was the fiftieth year, when land returned to its original family owners (Leviticus 25:8–17).
